methodology: Nonwovens were produced using the air-laid process from a blend of milkweed fibers and polylactic acid (PLA) fibers. Some non-wovens were compressed to investigate their thermal, acoustic, and mechanical properties under various conditions.
research_objective: To develop acoustic insulating carpets from milkweed fibers using an air-laid spike process for the automotive industry, with a focus on reducing noise pollution and environmental impact.

key_findings.finding: Milkweed and PLA carpets have lower thermal conductivity values of 37.45 (mW/m·K) compared to cotton and polypropylene carpets.
At high frequencies, milkweed and PLA carpets show sound absorption values of at least 0.6, providing better acoustic insulation than non-woven materials made from jute and polyethylene (PE) fibers.
Milkweed fibers exhibit excellent thermal and acoustic insulation properties due to their wide lumen and thin wall.
The sound absorption coefficient of nonwovens containing milkweed fibers increases with the percentage of milkweed fiber, attributed to the hollow structure and low density of milkweed fibers.
Air-laid process results in a significant reduction of fiber loss compared to carding process, with only 10% loss for milkweed fibers.
The air-laid process is carried out in a closed chamber while the carding process is performed in an open chamber, which explains the difference in fiber loss.
